newsitem.title: USA: Rain, high winds, hail batter Kansas wheat - WSC.
newsitem.headline: Rain, high winds, hail batter Kansas wheat - WSC.

text.p: Many Kansas wheat fields were battered by rain, high winds and hail late Wednesday, and more rain was forecast through the weekend, said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist.
"This was very unfavorable for the harvest," said Burgio.

Rain amounts of 0.5 to 1.5 inches fell over much of southwest and central Kansas, with greater amounts in localized areas. These storms also featured 60- to 70-mph winds and one- to 1-3/4-inch hail, which Burgio said probably knocked down the ripe wheat.
Wednesday's storm system should move into Oklahoma Thursday, but another storm system will enter Kansas late Thursday or Friday producing rain through Saturday, he said.
"There will be more storms and thunderstorms in the region for the next several days, causing more problems for the wheat harvest," he said.
The first chance of an extended dry spell in the Kansas wheat areas appeared to be late next week, Burgio said.
